title: Mandatory reporting obligations that institutions routinely ignore
p1:
Many institutions have rules on paper that look impressive. The surprising part? Some of the most critical duties are ignored when reporting a problem becomes uncomfortable.

Mandatory reporting is not just a policy statement. In many situations, it is a legal responsibility to report specific concerns, such as abuse, safety risks, financial wrongdoing, or serious misconduct, to the proper authorities.
p2:
A common misconception is that an institution can handle every issue internally. That is not always true. When the law requires a report, delaying, hiding, or quietly resolving the matter may create a bigger problem than the original incident.

One thing many people do not realize: the obligation often falls on the individual who becomes aware of the issue, not only on senior management.
p3:
The practical lesson is simple: having a reporting policy is not the same as following it. Organizations need clear procedures, trained staff, and a culture where reporting concerns is treated as responsibility, not disloyalty.

Knowing when a report is mandatory can protect individuals and institutions from serious consequences.
conclusion: Have you ever seen an organization ignore a reporting responsibility because it was inconvenient? What should institutions do differently?
